Phil Stutz is a psychiatrist, and Jonah Hill, who is his patient, made the film
about him. What separates Stutz from the therapy the film sets him against is
that he hands over **tools**: short visualizations to be used at the moment the
difficulty arrives, rather than insights arrived at slowly over years. His
starting claim is that three conditions cannot be escaped by anybody, so a
usable method has to work in their presence: pain, uncertainty, and the
requirement to keep working.

## Concepts

- **Part X.** The inner voice that blocks action and passes judgement. Stutz
  treats it as permanent rather than curable, so the work is to act against it
  repeatedly instead of waiting for it to quieten.
- **The String of Pearls.** Each action is one pearl on a string, and every
  pearl counts the same. Doing the thing counts for more than doing it well.
  Each pearl also contains a dot, the imperfection that arrives with any act.
- **The Shadow.** The part of yourself you are ashamed of. It is addressed by
  facing it and speaking to it, which removes the effort spent hiding it.
- **The Maze.** Being held up by comparison with somebody else, waiting for a
  fairness that is not coming. The exit is an act of your own rather than a
  settlement.
- **Radical acceptance.** Look for what can be taken from an adverse event
  instead of contesting that it happened.
